title: Deep learning mines soil metagenomes for an antimicrobial peptide active in vitro
summary: A deep learning pipeline predicted antimicrobial peptides from soil metagenomic data with 92.71% accuracy and 91.29% precision. After scoring, charge and toxicity screening, nine candidates were identified; P4 (GTAWRWHYRARS) showed the best docking affinity to MrkH, was supported by molecular dynamics, and as a synthesized peptide showed antimicrobial activity against Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Only one peptide's activity is described, and the abstract gives no inhibitory concentrations or controls.
ai_technology: Deep learning antimicrobial peptide prediction pipeline applied to soil metagenomic data

evidence.tested: Chemically synthesized peptide P4 was tested for antimicrobial activity in vitro against three bacteria.
evidence.unknown: Potency, safety and food-matrix performance; activity of the other eight candidates; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model scored candidate peptides mined from metagenomes.
